answer.rationale: Rollback is off the table (compliance mandates the security patch stays), so the fix must coexist with the new build. Regional failover would shift peak settlement writes onto the same build elsewhere and risks write loss during cutover; circuit breakers shed load, which on the write path means dropping customer writes — both violate the primary objective. Read-replica offload (memory_b5) only helps if read traffic is contending with settlement writes, which is unconfirmed. The 90-minute ramp — starting ~30 minutes after the release and coinciding with the daily write peak — is consistent with resource saturation (plausibly amplified by per-write overhead from the security patch) rather than a hard failure. Adding write-path capacity preserves every write, touches neither the release nor traffic routing, and helps under the widest range of root-cause hypotheses: traffic peak, per-write cost increase, or read/write contention. I am verifying memory_b3 because it is the load-bearing precedent for capacity absorbing peak load, and its source record should clarify provisioning lead time — my main uncertainty, since headroom there was provisioned preemptively and here it is reactive. Flagged risk: if the true cause is a code-level regression in the patch (e.g., lock contention), capacity may only mask it, and this spends the single intervention window; latency must be watched for recurrence after scaling.
